relevant_findings.topic: Repaint garage doors require condition assessment before prep begins
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike NC (known substrate state), repaint garage doors require on-site condition assessment: visual inspection of existing coating (chalking, peeling, rust spots on steel, wood rot/moisture), adhesion testing (ASTM D3359 cross-hatch), and identification of existing coating type (latex vs oil). Assessment results drive prep intensity, primer selection, and round configuration. Steel doors with sound factory paint may need only degloss + spot prime, while failing paint requires full scrape + prime.

relevant_findings.topic: Three substrates with distinct repaint protocols — steel, wood, composite
relevant_findings.finding: Steel: degloss + scuff sand (sound) or scrape + feather-edge (failing) or rust debridement SSPC-SP3 (surface rust). DTM primer mandatory — wax contamination from original factory forming still present even in repaint context (wax migrates into primer film over time). Wood: TSP wash, scrape/sand as needed, six-side seal verification (historically missed — check bottom rail and hinge edges). Composite (carriage overlays): mixed-material assessment — steel base may have different condition than composite overlay panels.

relevant_findings.topic: Four substrate states drive prep intensity for garage door repaint
relevant_findings.finding: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (1.00x prep): scuff sand, spot prime thin areas. SS_EXT_CHALKING (1.20x prep): chalk remediation wash + chalk-binding primer. SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (1.50x prep): scrape failing areas, feather-edge sand, spot or full prime. SS_EXT_SURFACE_RUST (2.00x prep, steel only): SSPC-SP3 rust debridement to bare metal, zinc-rich or DTM primer on bare areas. Chalking is more common on garage doors than entry doors due to large sun-exposed flat surfaces.

relevant_findings.topic: Leapfrog technique remains critical for RP — articulation joint paint bridging is the primary failure mode
relevant_findings.finding: The leapfrog technique (paint alternating panels 1,3,5 then 2,4,6) is equally critical for repaint as NC. In fact, repaint increases the risk of joint bridging because existing paint film adds thickness. Articulation joints must be opened and verified tack-free between panel sets. Any bridged joints discovered during post-coat inspection must be scored with a utility knife before the next coat.

relevant_findings.topic: Bottom seal management is identical to NC — remove/prop/reinstall lifecycle
relevant_findings.finding: Bottom weatherseal (astragal) management for repaint follows the same lifecycle: remove before prep (or mask with low-tack tape), prop door 2-4 inches open during 24-48 hr cure, reinstall after cure. In repaint context, the existing seal may be degraded — assess condition and recommend replacement if cracked or hardened. Seal replacement is NOT in painting scope but should be flagged.

relevant_findings.topic: Door size remains primary cost driver — single vs double
relevant_findings.finding: Door size modifier carries over from NC spec. Single door (56-63 SF) = 1.00x baseline. Double door (112-126 SF) = 1.85x. Setup/cleanup has some fixed overhead per door regardless of size. Repaint adds assessment and condition-driven prep that scales with door area, making the size modifier slightly more impactful for failing/rust conditions.

relevant_findings.topic: QT3-QT4 range — same as NC (QT2 excluded, QT5 excluded)
relevant_findings.finding: Garage doors maintain the narrow 2-tier quality range for repaint. QT2 excluded because garage doors are visible from street. QT5 excluded because garage doors are utility surfaces, not architectural showcases. QT3 = standard production pace, 6-foot visual inspection, no intercoat sand. QT4 = premium pace, raking light at 3 feet, 220-grit intercoat sand, premium materials.

relevant_findings.topic: Skip-prime path for sound paint on steel — key difference from NC
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike NC where ALL steel garage doors require DTM primer (wax contamination on factory finish), repaint of steel doors with sound existing paint (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT) that passes adhesion testing may use a spot-prime-only approach. The wax contamination concern from NC is mitigated because the existing paint film has already sealed over the wax. However, any scraped or bare areas on steel still require DTM primer for rust inhibition.

relevant_findings.topic: Driveway/apron protection — canvas only, NO poly sheeting
relevant_findings.finding: Driveway protection requirement carries over from NC. Canvas drops or absorbent mats ONLY — standard poly sheeting is PROHIBITED on hardscapes due to slippery safety hazard. This is a project safety rule, not a quality preference. Spray application generates overspray that stains concrete permanently — protection is mandatory for spray, recommended for brush.

relevant_findings.topic: No fiberglass substrate for garage doors — steel/wood/composite only
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike entry doors (steel/fiberglass/wood), garage doors do not have a fiberglass substrate option. Sectional garage doors are steel (90%+), wood (traditional), or carriage-style (steel base with composite overlay panels). The composite overlays may be fiberglass-reinforced polyester (FRP), polyurethane foam, or vinyl — all treated as 'composite' requiring bonding primer when the surface is slick or sealed.

relevant_findings.topic: Repaint production rates — 30-50% premium over NC base rates
relevant_findings.finding: Garage door repaint adds condition assessment, existing coating removal (scraping, sanding), and more complex surface preparation compared to NC. Industry standard repaint premium for garage doors is 30-50%: sound paint ~30% premium (minimal extra prep), failing paint ~50% premium (significant scraping and feathering), surface rust ~80-100% premium (SSPC debridement is labor-intensive). These premiums apply to the core painting tasks, not setup/cleanup which is similar to NC.

relevant_findings.topic: Lead-safe RRP gate — pre-1978 garage doors may contain lead paint
relevant_findings.finding: Pre-1978 garage doors may have lead-based paint, especially on steel doors that received alkyd primers and enamels. Lead paint testing is required for pre-1978 structures per EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745). Positive test activates RRP containment for all paint disturbance tasks. However, pre-1978 garage doors are relatively uncommon in the current market — most garage doors have been replaced since then. This is a safety gate, not a common scenario.

relevant_findings.topic: Sheens for RP: satin and semi-gloss only (gloss excluded)
relevant_findings.finding: For repaint, gloss is excluded because it requires perfect substrate preparation that is rarely achievable over existing paint. Satin is the most common choice for garage doors (forgiving of substrate imperfections). Semi-gloss is available for QT4 premium work. This is a key difference from NC which allows satin/semi-gloss/gloss.

quality_tiers.rationale: QT2 excluded — garage doors are visible from street. QT5 excluded — utility surface, not architectural showcase.

application_methods.rationale: Spray is primary (large flat panels). Brush for detail/recesses. Roller PROHIBITED on metal doors (orange peel). Back-rolling NOT applicable to metal doors.

sheens.rationale: Gloss excluded for RP — requires substrate perfection not achievable over existing paint.

substrate_materials.notes: Steel is dominant (~90%). Wood is traditional/premium. Composite refers to carriage overlay panels (FRP, polyurethane, vinyl).

substrate_states.notes: 4 repaint states. SS_EXT_CHALKING added for RP (common on large flat surfaces). SS_EXT_SURFACE_RUST is steel-only.

zones.notes: Canvas drops — NOT poly. Safety hazard on hardscapes.
Track, rollers, springs, cables — must not be painted.
Bottom seal remove/mask + prop during cure + reinstall.

research_corrections.original_claim: Steel RP always requires full DTM primer like NC
research_corrections.corrected_to: Repaint of steel with SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT and passing adhesion test can use spot-prime-only approach. Wax contamination concern from NC is mitigated by existing sealed paint film. Bare/scraped areas still require DTM primer for rust inhibition.

research_corrections.original_claim: Environmental conditions should be estimation modifiers
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable — unpredictable at bid time. Excluded from spec entirely per PaintFactor OS RC-003.
